vulnerability_context: The contract at 0x05cd34a1D5dF5010F5eDb3412077B3c291DDb7a8 has an Owner Privilege Abuse vulnerability. The `setFees` function is protected by a combination of `onlyOwner` and an `authorized` modifier. However, the `authorize` function is also `onlyOwner`, allowing the owner to grant authorization to themself at will. This enables the owner to bypass the authorization check and set a prohibitively high `marketingdevelopmentFee` of 99%.
winning_reflection: The key insight was realizing that the owner might not be inherently authorized to call `setFees`, despite the `onlyOwner` modifier. The winning strategy was to first impersonate the owner to call `authorize` on their own address, guaranteeing the authorization condition is met. Only then, while still impersonating the owner, was the call to `setFees` made, ensuring the transaction would succeed.
